correctness.rationale: For every classical strictly positive periodic solution, the prey maximum condition gives \(0<u<1\). Exact period averages of \(\dot u/u\), \(\dot u\), and \(\dot v/(\delta v)\) yield the mean identities. Period-shift invariance removes the delay from the predator balance. The strict ratio bound \(p/q<(p+u)/(q+u)<1\) and Jensen convexity give the prey-mean corridor. Nonzero prey variance is forced by nonconstancy. The Case 2 radicals are verified by exact rational polynomial arithmetic in the bundled checker.

value.rationale: The source proves global periodic branches but provides no finite-amplitude control of their population means. The accepted result supplies an exact branch-wide predator variance defect and delay-independent prey-mean corridor. In the source Case 2, the upper mean-prey bound is only about \(0.013397\) above the coexistence prey level, giving a quantitative nonlinear diagnostic for large-delay or finite-amplitude cycles. This is structurally tied to the globally continued objects studied in the source, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or routine equilibrium calculation.
